text: Mind the nets. They're older than you and twice as tangled.
Hesk. I mend what the sea chews up, and I tell anyone who'll stand still how to catch a fish.

menu.text: Ask away. My hands keep working either way.

choices.text: Where do I get a rod?

text: Rod in your equipment slot, face open water, {key_interact} to cast. A shore, a pier, the rail of a ship, all the same to a fish.
Watch the float. A nibble or two, then it dips with a splash. {key_interact} right then. Too soon and you pull the hook out of its mouth. Too late and it's gone.
Marlo sells driftwood rods at the market, and worms with them. Start there.
A better rod casts further, gets a bite sooner and gives you longer to strike. Bamboo, then steel-tipped. The master's rods turn up in old chests, if you're lucky.
Click your bait in the bag and it goes on the hook. No bait and you're fishing a bare hook: slow, and only the stupid ones bite.
Shrimp brings the rarer ones. Glow bait's best by night. Short of it? Cut your own on the action wheel from a crab or a fish and a bit of kelp.
What bites depends on the water under your float, the coast and the hour. Shallow water, small fish.
End of the pier for the deep ones. The cove at dawn. And every island out there has its own, so fish wherever you drop anchor.
Then you've got a fight. Hold to reel and the line tightens. Let go when it runs, or it snaps.
Let it go slack too long and it throws the hook. Reel when it rests. Patience. Fish have more of it than captains.

bye.text: Bring me a torn net sometime. I'll make it worse and charge you.
